comparisons.peer_topic: Acquisition of ZT Systems: Manufacturing Business Strategy
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD intends to seek a strategic partner to acquire ZT Systems' manufacturing business as part of the acquisition.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD disclose strategic moves involving manufacturing capabilities and business unit alignment in fiscal 2024, though the specific actions differ. Intel established an internal foundry operating model to separate design (Intel Products) from manufacturing (Intel Foundry), creating an internal customer-supplier relationship for its own CPUs. AMD, conversely, disclosed an intent to sell off its manufacturing business assets acquired via the ZT Systems acquisition to seek a strategic partner, indicating a divestiture or outsourcing strategy for manufacturing rather than an internal separation. Intel's approach integrates manufacturing within the corporate structure under a new operating model, while AMD's approach involves exiting specific manufacturing assets.

sentences.text: We previously announced the implementation of our internal foundry operating model, which took effect in the first quarter of 2024, and creates a foundry relationship between our Intel Products business (collectively CCG, DCAI, and NEX) and our Intel Foundry business.

Intel Foundry consists substantially of process engineering, manufacturing, and foundry services groups that provide manufacturing, test, and assembly services to our Intel Products business and to external customers.
The Company intends to seek a strategic partner to acquire ZT Systems' manufacturing business.

peer_results.rationale: The available candidates (acquisition of Seagate SoC operations and sale of EUC business) concern M&A and divestitures unrelated to Intel's internal foundry operating model restructuring. No candidate addresses internal manufacturing organizational changes or segment definitions related to foundry services.

The available candidates define specific business units (CNBU and EBU) but do not disclose any restructuring of manufacturing versus design operations, nor do they mention an internal foundry model. The disclosures are static definitions of reporting segments rather than structural changes to manufacturing relationships.
